Quantum Phantoms (live document)

Live document: it tracks the progress of the reverse-engineering work and is rebuilt from the letter READMEs and status.json as targets move. States, ratings and numbers will change.

What we aim to achieve: synthetic lung tumours inside real 3-D chest CT that are realistic enough to train cancer-detection AI, controlled enough to test it on exactly the cases it misses, and traceable enough that a clinician or regulator can trust the result.

Why it matters. Detection models fail most on the cases real data has least of: tiny, ground-glass, and wall- or vessel-touching nodules, usually without exact ground truth, follow-up scans or the right to share them. Synthetic tumours with exact masks, chosen difficulty and a baseline and follow-up scan can fill that gap without using any patient voxels. They are only trustworthy if every step rests on a published, reproduced method and every case can be traced back to how it was made. If the pipeline reaches clinical validation, it can bring better-trained and better-tested lung-cancer detection forward by a few years. extrapolation

Why quantum. The plan is to build one large quantum circuit that maps how a tumour starts growing: in D the first cell lineage and tissue patch grow through entangled quantum dynamics on IBM's heavy-hex chip. It runs at 21 qubits in simulation today; the planned 108-qubit version aims beyond classical simulation (claim level L2, plan and conditions). speculative C certifies every tumour draw with a Bell test, and B draws site and tumour type together in one quantum circuit. evidence-based

Disclaimer. At today's sizes the quantum stages can still be simulated classically, on laptops or supercomputers, so this work builds a quantum pipeline that is ready when hardware outgrows them. See the Future and its claim ladder.

Why reverse-engineer

For every stage, some published method already solves part of the problem: a Bayesian-network compiler, Bell-test entropy accounting, quantum causal-state models, Pixel2Cancer, scanner fingerprinting, VICTRE and others. Rebuilding each method ourselves, from the paper and without copying proprietary code, gives us components we understand, can cite, and can adapt to lungs. Every target goes through the same lifecycle:

  1. Dissect: a dossier with method, equations, parameters and claimed result.
  2. Reproduce: match one published number or figure in repro/ before changing anything.
  3. Adapt: to lungs, 3-D, certification and our contracts.
  4. Integrate, or reject with a written reason.

States move listed → dissected → reproduced → adapted → integrated | rejected, recorded per letter in <L>_<name>/status.json and shown as badges in the target table.

Privacy by construction

No patient voxels enter any generator. Host CT scans (LIDC-IDRI, later Mayo Siemens raw data) are only read: to choose a site, measure the scanner fingerprint, and insert into. The tumor's appearance comes from fitted parameters (shape, edge profile, HU per nodule type) and published statistics only. Learned refiners trained on patients (DiffTumor, MAISI) appear only as ablations.
